tasks.title: Reserved capacity for a steady load
tasks.statement: The load is steady: 4000 requests per second around the clock. The servers are paid for on demand. Switch them to the reserved pricing (the “Pricing” parameter is shown in this exercise) for a discount of about 40% and stay within $1000 per month at a load of at most 80%.
tasks.hint: Eight M servers on demand cost 960 for servers alone — over 1200 with the database and load balancer. With reservation it is about 580 for servers.

tasks.title: Spot instances for workers
tasks.statement: Order processing goes through a queue, and the workers tolerate interruption: the message returns to the queue. Switch the workers to spot (three times cheaper), make processing idempotent, and keep at least two workers. Load at most 85%, the queue drains without lag (peak of 10 s, 5 s allowed), and the budget is $1200 per month.
tasks.hint: Three M workers handle 1200 per second at a load of 900. On spot they cost about 72 per month instead of 240.

tasks.title: Servers that are too big
tasks.statement: The service gets 2400 requests per second, and the diagram has six L servers (capacity 9000): they are only 27% loaded, and the bill is huge. Pick the right size: server load at most 80%, but no more — the budget is $1100 per month for the whole design (the database is an M with a replica).
tasks.hint: Two L servers give 3000 requests — 80%. Four M servers give 2800: 86% — too much.

tasks.title: A CDN is cheaper than servers
tasks.statement: The site serves 12,000 static requests per second through the app servers, so they have to be kept with plenty of headroom. Add a CDN (≥90%) and recalculate the fleet: load at most 80%, budget $450 per month for the whole design.
tasks.hint: With a CDN, static content barely reaches the servers: two M servers are enough. The CDN costs 60 per month, while an extra M server costs 120.

tasks.title: The same service, cheaper
tasks.statement: The chapter's final exercise. A shop: 6000 requests per second (1000 static through a CDN, the rest dynamic), with orders going through a queue. Cut the bill without losing reliability: reserved pricing for the app servers, spot for the idempotent workers, a CDN (≥90%), survival of a zone failure and a server failure, load at most 80%, and a budget of $3000 per month.
tasks.hint: Nine M servers in three zones (after losing a zone six remain — 4200) on reserved pricing; three M workers on spot in three zones; an M database with three replicas and automatic failover in three zones (after losing a zone two replicas remain — 6000 reads).
